lines.t: Question. Are the volumes of truth and, adding to, the Bible?
Answer. Yes and no. Yes, because they are the word of the Lord and are in perfect agreement
with the Bible, having the very same author, the Lord himself. No, because I myself, have not added
to the Bible. My friends, I do not wish to replace, or take away, or add to the Bible.
rather these words and this understanding was given to me by the lord and is for all those
who have ears to hear he alone may add to his word for our benefit and to give us greater
understanding i hear this question from churches and other christians frequently
and they use this as an excuse to discount the volumes of truth but if their assertion holds
true, that no one should, add to, the words of the Bible, then the Bible should have been a very
short book indeed, also making the Lord a hypocrite, since every consecutive book of the
Bible was literally added to the Bible. The entire NT was added to the Bible, hence the name,
the New Testament. Not to mention, every translation of the Bible is a form of adding
to and taking away from the Bible, not only of words, but also some of the meaning, glory,
and impact is lost in translation. Thus when the Lord said not add to or take away from his word,
what did he really mean? The following verse is worn against, adding to, God's word. In order to
obey the mitzvot, word, of Adonai your God which I am giving you, do not add to what I am saying,
and do not subtract from it. Deuteronomy chapter 4 verse 2. Everything I am commanding you,
you are to take care to do. Do not add to it or subtract from it. Deuteronomy chapter 12 verse 32.
Don't add anything to his words, or he will rebuke you, and you be found a liar.
Proverbs chapter 30 verse 6. I warn everyone hearing the words of the prophecy in this book
that if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues written in this book.
Revelation chapter 22 verse 18. These verses clearly say not to add to God's word,
yet do not mention not adding to the Bible. If this were true, then the Bible should have ended
at Deuteronomy chapter 4 verse 2. It is very clear that each consecutive book of the Bible is an
adding to. Neither did the Israelites interpret these verses as not adding to the Bible,
otherwise each consecutive prophet would have been labeled, false.
Under the incorrect interpretation of the verses above, Yahushua is the most guilty of all.
So then, not tampering with as implied, especially in Revelation chapter 22 verse 18.
But the overarching meaning, intention, theme of these verses in Deuteronomy,
Proverbs, and Revelation was to not add to or take away from what the Word of God is actually
saying or what the Lord was commanding, according to man's understanding. As in don't try to
interpret or rationalize the Word of the Lord in such a way that excuses, allows, encourages
disobedience, or purposefully misinterprets or ignores certain verses to uphold a certain way
of doing things. Holding on to private church doctrines and the commandments of men, putting
ourselves and our personal wants, desires, above God and his commands.
First of all, understand this. No prophecy of scripture is to be interpreted by an individual
on his own. For never has a prophecy come as a result of human willing. On the contrary,
people moved by the Ruach HaKadosh, Holy Spirit, spoke a message from God.
God. 2 Peter chapter 1 verses 20-21. Asterisk but the person who has the spirit can evaluate
everything, while no one is in a position to evaluate him. For who has known the mind of
Adonai? Who will counsel him? But we have the mind of the Messiah. 1 Corinthians chapter 2 verse 15.
Therefore, to hold on to this idea that no one should, add to, or, take away, from the Bible,
according to men, is true. However, the Lord himself, may add to his own word. The rule of,
adding to, and, taking away, does not apply to the Lord, himself. Otherwise, he would have
contradicted his own command every time he sent a prophet to proclaim his word to the people.
The Lord, alone, may add to his word and the Bible, we may not. Most often times, the Lord
spoke to his prophets who were to proclaim his message to the people which was then later added
to the bible on the contrary people moved by the ruach har kadesh holy spirit spoke a message from

You shall grow strong and proclaim my word to those who are near and to those afar off.
You shall speak to the believer and unbeliever alike, and declare my judgments against the

For I tell you the truth, the translations of men are greatly erred, which leads to an even
